proposals.detectability_argument: With the arm guard gone a FIRE with no preceding arm pulses prog_en; any test that FIREs unarmed and watches prog_en kills it.

proposals.mutated_code: if (a > 7'h05) err = 1'b1; if (a == A_FIRE && arm) do_fire = 1'b1;
proposals.detectability_argument: A READ of address 0x78 while armed pulses; the unknown-address read test and the armed command-byte sweep observe prog_en.
A write to 0x79 while armed pulses; the command-byte sweep while armed sees prog_en.
A write to 0x7A while armed pulses; the command-byte sweep while armed sees prog_en.
A second FIRE (and any register write) during the pulse is no longer rejected, so it reloads the pulse counter and the measured pulse length exceeds PULSE_WIDTH; PROTOCOL_ERROR is also not set.
A 17- or 18-bit frame commits as a normal frame instead of PROTOCOL_ERROR; the overlong-frame tests see a PERR miss or a committed write/pulse.
A 15-bit frame commits; the truncated-frame tests see a missing PROTOCOL_ERROR or a register change.
Wrong-length frames no longer set PROTOCOL_ERROR; bad_frame_length_sets_protocol_error reads STATUS and misses the flag.
